title: SSE session fencing and deterministic output markers to prevent split/partial responses
creator: Ava Chen
description: Several customers reported split or truncated SSE streams when mid-request failures (node preemption, network flaps) happen. Symptoms: client receives a partial logical response (missing last-turn tokens), or receives duplicated suffix tokens after resume from a reconnect. This ticket implements a session fencing and deterministic-output-marker approach so clients can: 1) detect whether a resumed connection will continue the same logical output or should request a replay, and 2) render deterministic finality markers so partial outputs never appear as "complete" in the UI. The scope is Hosted API streaming; solution must be compatible with Dedicated and Private (backwards-compatible handshake), and include server-side repair/backfill paths for short-term customer recovery.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Chen: Escalation triaged. Affected customers: fintech-corp (high-volume chat), product-ops (analytics pipeline). Initial investigation points to interleaved session state when a worker recovers mid-request.

2026-03-03 - Miguel Torres: Spike completed. Prototype uses monotonic session_epoch + per-chunk sequence numbers. Added deterministic-output-marker token '<<STREAM-FINAL:epoch.seq>>' emitted once server guarantees finality for the logical response.
2026-03-05 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Customers accept short-term client update if server-side backfill is delivered within 72 hours. Prioritize compatibility with JS/Swift SDKs.
2026-03-08 - Eng review: Kernel scheduling edge-case found where KV-cache rebind on worker swap caused duplicate last tokens. Will introduce fencing + atomic commit during drain.

2026-03-10 - Miguel Torres: Draft PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4256. Includes session fencing, sequence handshake, and server-assisted replay endpoint. Needs load simulation results.

2026-03-12 - QA: Integration smoke shows 99.98% reduction in split-response incidents on synthetic preempt tests. Two flaky cases remain when client reconnects with mismatched epoch header; adding clearer client guidance.
2026-03-14 - Security review requested. PR attached for SSO/KMS impact review; markers do not expose secrets but timing channels need evaluation.
Next steps: finish end-to-end SDK changes, ship runtime patch in runtime-1.20 as hotfix, and run customer backfill for impacted request IDs.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits epoch+sequence-based session headers for every streaming response and includes deterministic finality marker when logical output is complete.
Client SDKs (JS + iOS) can resume by sending last-seen epoch.seq; server either resumes from that point or instructs client to perform a replay.
No customer-visible duplicated token sequences in 99.9% of synthetic preempt/reconnect scenarios (measured runway load test).
Post-deploy: provide a one-time backfill tool to deliver missing final chunks for affected request IDs within 72 hours of deployment.
Security sign-off completed for marker scheme and any API additions (no secret leakage or elevated attack surface).
implementation_plan: Design: finalize session-fencing protocol (epoch, seq, signed resume token) - Miguel + Research (2026-03-02 to 2026-03-04).
Runtime: implement atomic session handoff with fencing guard and deterministic finality marker emit (runtime team) - PR #4256.
API: add optional 'Resume-Epoch' and 'Resume-Seq' headers and /v1/streams/:id/replay endpoint for server-assisted replay/backfill.
SDK: update JS and iOS streaming clients to parse epoch/seq and fallback to non-streaming fetch when server requires replay.
QA: extend chaos tests to include worker preempt, network partition, and deliberate response duplicate injection. Run load tests at production QPS. (estimate 2 days)
Deploy: staged rollout on hosted API with feature flag; monitor streaming error rate + duplication metrics; enable backfill for top 3 impacted customers.
Postmortem: capture incidents, customer communication notes, and recommend Dedicated/Private config guidance.
test_plan: Unit tests: validate epoch/seq encoding/decoding and marker detection logic.
Integration: simulate mid-request worker replacement and assert client either resumes or receives replay instruction.
Chaos: run chaos-suite with 10k streaming requests including node preemption; measure split/duplicate token rate.
Customer regression: run affected customer traffic snapshot in staging and run through client SDK resume flows.
Performance: ensure session fencing adds <2ms median latency to the first 512 tokens path and no observable throughput regressions at 95th percentile.
Security: threat-model change to check timing channels and header integrity; include SRE/SEC sign-off.
risks: Client adoption: older SDKs may not interpret epoch/seq and could show partial outputs as complete. Mitigation: server returns explicit NON-RESUMABLE flag for older clients.
Latency: extra handshake may add small overhead to first bytes; mitigate by piggybacking on existing streaming handshake and benchmarking.

Backfill consistency: reconstructing missing final tokens for large responses may require replaying model generation which could be non-deterministic across model variants. Mitigation: server uses checkpointed KV cache snapshots where possible and falls back to best-effort transcript reconstruction with customer consent.
Operational: staged rollout must include fast rollback path if duplication increases; keep feature flag ready.
